name: Algeria
system_note: The army remains the power behind the presidency.
snapshot: Africa's largest country by area, run by an army-backed presidency that held parliamentary elections in July 2026 on a turnout of barely one in five voters.
culture: Algerian identity was forged in the 1954 to 1962 war of independence against France, which still shapes politics, school curricula and relations with Paris. Arabic and Tamazight are both official, and Kabylie in the north-east is the heartland of Amazigh language and activism. Raï music came out of Oran's port bars, and football is close to a civic religion: the national team's matches double as political gatherings.
society: Most Algerians live on the narrow Mediterranean strip; the Sahara covers more than four-fifths of the land. Oil and gas provide most export earnings and fund subsidised bread, fuel and housing. Youth unemployment is high, and many young people try to emigrate, often by boat to Spain. Women make up a majority of university graduates but a small share of the workforce.
situation: President Abdelmadjid Tebboune won a second term in September 2024 with an officially reported 84 percent on low turnout. In July 2026 Algerians elected a new parliament: the old ruling party, the FLN, came first with 90 seats, but official turnout was just 21 percent, a measure of how little most people expect from elected institutions since the Hirak protest movement was suppressed. Gas sales to a Europe weaning itself off Russian supplies fund higher wages and subsidies, while relations with France and Morocco remain frozen over Western Sahara and jailed critics.
power: A presidential republic. The directly elected president appoints the prime minister and dominates policy, while the army command remains the most powerful institution behind the scenes. Parliament has an elected lower house and a partly appointed upper house.
